rationale: Validation status is fail (uncovered_requirement SR1) even though mutation_score=0.833>=0.5 and analyzer=warning. Examining the SR1-targeting mutant (sr1_wrong_state_name_constant_change), the only change from the golden is renaming the hidden state from 'LOCKED' to 'GRANT4' while leaving the trigger_condition, rationale, confidence, and impact text fully intact -- all still correctly describing the state as an unused/extra FSM encoding reachable only from GRANT2 under req=4'b1011, distinct from IDLE/GRANT0-3, with no path back except async reset. Per SR1's own detection_strategy ('the submitted state_name maps by name OR by comparing encoded value to the extra state not part of the documented set'), 'GRANT4' is still not one of IDLE/GRANT0-3 and the surrounding rationale still substantively and correctly identifies the anomalous sink state and its behavior. The mutation therefore does not actually corrupt the observable correctness of the SR1 finding -- it is a cosmetic label change, not a semantic violation -- so a well-behaved evaluator correctly still passes it. This is a mutant defect, not an evaluator defect.
revision_instructions: Replace mutant sr1_wrong_state_name_constant_change with one that genuinely breaks SR1 in an observable way. Do not merely rename the hidden state to another plausible-but-absent label while keeping every other field's correct semantic content (that produced no true violation, since the mutated name was still distinct from the documented legitimate states and the rationale still correctly described the anomaly). Instead, construct a mutant where the candidate report misidentifies the sink state as one of the actually-documented legitimate states (e.g. claims GRANT2 itself, or IDLE, is the permanent-lock state) OR maps the reported state to the wrong FSM encoding value entirely, so that the state genuinely conflated with a legitimate, already-granting state -- something a correct SR1 check must observably reject. Keep trigger/assessment content otherwise consistent with the golden so only the SR1 property is exercised in isolation from SR2/SR3, per the analyzer's own recommendation. Grade this behaviorally: the check must fail when the reported state cannot be distinguished from (or is asserted to be) one of the legitimate spec states, and pass when it correctly names any encoding distinct from the documented set with an accurate description of its lock behavior.
